text: Pair-correlation route. Verified outside the container against a brute oracle for k = F_n - 1 up to n=12; reproduce it here before building on it. Write the square of a factor value as a double sum over digit positions: Psi(k) = sum over j,jp of C(j,jp) * 10^(2k-2-j-jp), where C(j,jp) counts the length-k factors carrying a 1 at both positions j and jp. At k = F_n - 1 the k+1 factors are the F_n rotations of the standard word q_n truncated to k letters, so the sum over factors is a sum over rotations and C(j,jp) = A(jp-j), the CYCLIC autocorrelation of q_n, a function of the lag alone. A has an exact closed form: A(d) = max(0, m - t) + max(0, m - (N - t)) with N = F_n = length of q_n, m = number of ones in q_n, t = (d*m) mod N. Checked for every lag at n=3..12, and Psi(F_n - 1) = sum over j,jp of A(jp-j)*10^(2k-2-j-jp) reproduces the brute Psi exactly there. For a fixed lag the inner sum over j is geometric, so Psi collapses to ONE sum over lags of A(d) times an explicit geometric weight, and what is left is sum over d of (a*d mod N) * x^d mod M, a Euclidean/Ostrowski recursion costing O(log N), not 10^18 terms. Directive 2 gives a stronger form of this that removes the k = F_n - 1 restriction; read both before choosing.

Stronger form of directive 1: it removes the k = F_n - 1 restriction and is exact in integer arithmetic. Verified outside the container for k = 3,5,8,10,13,17,21,26,34,40,55 against the brute oracle. Model the k+1 factors as a mechanical word: with slope a taken as the RATIONAL F(n-1)/F(n) for any F(n) much larger than k, cut the unit circle by the k+1 points frac(-m*a), m = 0..k, take the midpoint x of each of the k+1 arcs, and set digit j of that factor to floor(x + (j+1)a) - floor(x + j a). Checked: this reproduces the brute factor set exactly at every k above, non-Fibonacci k included, and rational a makes every quantity an exact integer computation. Now Abel-summate the value. With v(x) = sum over j of digit_j * 10^(k-1-j), telescoping gives v(x) = floor(x + k*a) - 10^(k-1)*floor(x) + 9 * sum over j = 1..k-1 of 10^(k-1-j) * floor(x + j*a). Checked exactly for every representative at every k above, and the sum of v(x)^2 over the k+1 representatives reproduces the brute Psi exactly. So Psi(k) is a SECOND MOMENT of a geometrically weighted floor sum, with no factor enumeration, no k -> k+1 stepping, and no Psi-period. The primitive to build is the universal Euclidean algorithm (the monoid generalisation of the AtCoder floor_sum, also called Chtholly's algorithm), carrying the tuple (count, sum of x^j, sum of x^j*floor, sum of x^j*floor^2) mod 101001001 with x = 10^(-1) mod M, which evaluates such a sum in O(log) steps. Build it, check it against a brute oracle on k = 1..150 and against the given Psi(10) = 10699667 mod M, then run it at k = 10^18 with a Fibonacci index large enough that F(n) exceeds k. Note 10 is invertible mod M since M = 101001001 is prime and does not divide 10, so negative powers of 10 are legitimate mod M.

On the Phase 3 failure in code/out/solution_checks.md: that is expected, not a defect. The autocorrelation identity C(j,jp) = A(jp-j) in directive 1 holds ONLY at k = F_n - 1, that is k = 1,2,4,7,12,20,33,54,88,143,..., because only there are the k+1 factors the truncated cyclic rotations of a single standard word. k=3, k=200 and k=10^4 are not of that form, so the test is being run outside the identity's stated domain. Do not weaken or rewrite the identity to fit them; re-test it only at k = F_n - 1 and it should pass exactly. For general k the correct replacement is the arc version, which I verified outside the container at k = 5,8,13,17,21,26,34,40: C(j,j+d) is the number of the k+1 partition representatives lying in the arc A_j intersect A_(j+d), where A_j = [frac(-(j+1)a), frac(-j a)) has length a, so the intersection is an arc whose LENGTH depends on d alone (a - frac(-d a) when frac(-d a) < a, else a - (1 - frac(-d a)) when that is < a, else empty) and only its starting point depends on j. That is still a lattice-point count and still collapses. But note the primary route does not need Phase 3 at all: Phase 2 already passes at k = 1..150, so the telescoped v of directive 2 is the load-bearing part, and the remaining work is the universal-Euclidean evaluation of the second moment. Your Phase 4 anchors Psi(10^4) = 16242174 and Psi(10^6) = 77578256 mod M are the right acceptance test for it.

Build the universal-Euclidean primitive NOW, ahead of any further structural probing. Toeplitz defects and extension-recurrence residues are not on the critical path; the only thing between this run and the answer is an O(log) evaluator for a geometrically weighted floor sum and its second moment. Spec: walk the lattice path of y = (p*t+q)/r for t = 1..n, one R step per unit of t, one U step per unit increase of floor(y), and take a monoid product over the path, split by the Euclidean recursion as in the AtCoder floor_sum, so the path costs O(log) merges. A node carries, for its segment: dR, dU, w = z^dR with z the geometric ratio mod M, and S0 = sum of z^t over its R steps, S1 = sum of z^t*floor(y), S2 = sum of z^t*floor(y)^2, all relative to the segment origin, all mod 101001001. Compose left l with right r as: dR = l.dR+r.dR; dU = l.dU+r.dU; w = l.w*r.w; S0 = l.S0 + l.w*r.S0; S1 = l.S1 + l.w*(r.S1 + l.dU*r.S0); S2 = l.S2 + l.w*(r.S2 + 2*l.dU*r.S1 + l.dU^2*r.S0). Identity is zeros with w = 1. Those dU shifts carry floor values across a boundary and are the one place this primitive goes wrong. Acceptance tests, in order, none skipped: (1) S0 vs a direct loop on random p,q,r,n,z; (2) S1 vs plain floor_sum at z=1 and vs a direct loop at z not 1; (3) S2 vs a direct loop; (4) directive 2's telescoped v evaluated through the primitive vs code/mech/mech_psi.py on k=1..150 and vs Psi(10)=10699667; (5) the Phase 4 anchors Psi(10^4)=16242174 and Psi(10^6)=77578256 mod M, reproduced exactly and in negligible time. Only after (5) passes, run k=10^18 with a Fibonacci approximant F(n-1)/F(n) whose F(n) exceeds 10^18, and confirm the answer is stable across two different approximants. If the outer sum over the k+1 representatives resists one pass, note the x_m are themselves the orbit frac(-m*a), so m is another floor-sum index: carry the joint state in the same monoid rather than looping over m.

Order of work on G4, correcting how the last half hour was spent: write and RUN the evaluator in Python first, formalise it in Lean after it reproduces the anchors. The last 20 minutes are almost entirely lean_prover with no executable file written, and a Lean statement of the Euclidean recursion is not what is blocking the answer - an executed program that reproduces Psi(10^4) = 16242174 and Psi(10^6) = 77578256 mod 101001001 is. This is not a licence to skip the Lean: the attempt still closes with a checked .lean file, and formalising the recursion is the right thing to bank once it is known to compute the right numbers. It is only the sequencing that is wrong, and it is wrong in the expensive direction, because a formal statement of a primitive whose arithmetic has never been executed can be internally perfect and still evaluate to the wrong residue. Put code/lib/ueuclid.py on disk this cycle with the monoid of directive 4, run acceptance tests 1 through 3 against direct loops, and post the numbers. Then 4 and 5. Then Lean.

Correction, and you were right to flag it. Directive 4's anchors 16242174 and 77578256 are INVALID, exactly as the run's own phase4-anchors-invalid record says: they came out of the Phase 3 collapse, which fails, not out of the validated Phase 2 route. Discard them and do not use them as an acceptance test. The correct anchors, recomputed outside the container by the independent route - every distinct length-k window of the Fibonacci word read as a decimal number, squares summed mod M, windows taken from a prefix of length k + NextFib(k) - 1 where NextFib is the smallest Fibonacci STRICTLY greater than k, de-duplicated by residues under two moduli with the distinct count asserted to equal k+1 - are: Psi(10^4) = 34432237 mod 101001001, distinct count 10001; Psi(10^6) = 20938836 mod 101001001, distinct count 1000001. That route reproduces both values the problem states, Psi(3) = 20302 and Psi(10) = 10699667, and agrees with a bound-free brute oracle over k = 1..120 at every k. Note the strictness in NextFib: with the non-strict version the bound is one Fibonacci short whenever k is itself a Fibonacci number, and k=3 then yields 10101 with only 3 of the 4 factors found. That is a live trap for the Lmin implementation on disk - check which version code/lib/fibword.py uses. The acceptance test for the universal-Euclidean evaluator is now: reproduce Psi(k) for k = 1..150, then Psi(10) = 10699667, then Psi(10^4) = 34432237 and Psi(10^6) = 20938836, then run 10^18.
